newsitem.title: UK: Albania sees GDP falling by 3-7 pct this year.
newsitem.headline: Albania sees GDP falling by 3-7 pct this year.

text.p: Albania's economy will contract by between three and seven percent this year as a result of the orgy of violence that has gripped the country in recent months, a senior government official said on Tuesday.

"All estimates are of course very preliminary because everything has happened so quickly," Edmond Leka, head of economic aid and development for Albania's council of ministers, said at the annual meeting of the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD).
"But we think GDP will fall by between three and seven percent this year," he said.

The implementation of market-oriented reforms in the wake of the collapse of communism in the early 1990s had led to gross domestic product (GDP) growth of around 10 percent a year in 1993 to 1995 and 5.5 percent in 1996, said Finance Minister Arben Malaj.
Economists have warned that Albania, already one of Europe's poorest countries, risks lurching from political to economic crisis if it does not quickly restore order after the recent chaos.
Its GDP in 1996 was $2.3 billion for a population of 3.2 million, Malaj said. Over half of GDP comes from agriculture with industry accounting for a mere 13 percent.

Malaj hoped the social unrest would diminish in the wake of elections scheduled for June. This should allow international bodies and investors to resume projects in Albania which have been scaled down or suspended as a result of the fighting.
Foreign direct investment had grown to $95 million at the end of 1996 from $45 million three years earlier, he said.
